classification.difficultyReason: Track fruit juice removed and replaced, generalise the resulting percentage and solve for a target concentration.

content.prompt: A container holds 1.25 litres of a fruit juice drink. This drink is 25% fruit juice and the remainder is water.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If 0.5 litres of the drink is poured out and replaced by 50% fruit juice drink, find the percentage of the contents of the container that is now fruit juice.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Fruit juice remaining} &= 0.25(1.25-0.5) = 0.1875\text{ L}\\\text{Fruit juice added} &= 0.50\times0.5 = 0.25\text{ L}\\\text{Final fruit juice} &= 0.1875+0.25 = 0.4375\text{ L}\\\text{Fruit juice percentage} &= \frac{0.4375}{1.25}\times100\%\\\text{Fruit juice percentage} &= 35\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If $x$ litres of the drink is poured out and replaced by 50% fruit juice drink, find the percentage of the drink in the container that is now fruit juice.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Final fruit juice} &= 0.25(1.25-x)+0.50x\\\text{Final fruit juice} &= 0.3125+0.25x\text{ L}\\\text{Fruit juice percentage} &= \frac{0.3125+0.25x}{1.25}\times100\%\\\text{Fruit juice percentage} &= (25+20x)\%\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: How many litres of the fruit juice drink has to be poured out and replaced by the 50% fruit juice drink for the percentage to increase to 41%?

answer.worked:
Let $x$ litres be replaced. Using part b,
$$\begin{align*}25+20x &= 41\\20x &= 16\\x &= 0.8\end{align*}$$
Replace $0.8$ litres.
